sowing.notes: Spring sowings in double rows 20 cm apart.
Autumn sowings of hardy varieties such as 'Aquadulce' crop earliest.

cropping.notes: Pick while the pods are plump but the beans are still soft.

lookOutFor: Tall plants flop in wind; support with canes and string.

pests.name: Black bean aphid
pests.signs: Dense black aphids on the shoot tips
pests.control: Pinch out the tips once the first pods have set; rub off small colonies by hand.

pests.name: Chocolate spot
pests.signs: Brown spots on the leaves, worse in damp weather
pests.control: Space plants well for airflow and avoid feeding with too much nitrogen.

wintering.notes: Autumn-sown plants overwinter; cover with fleece in hard frost.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – broad beans; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow outside once the soil has warmed and frosts are over.

cropping.notes: Pick every few days, before the beans swell, to keep plants cropping.

lookOutFor: Flowers fail to set pods in hot, dry spells; water the roots well.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Young plants grazed overnight, slime trails
pests.control: Plant out sturdy plants, check after dark, and protect seedlings with barriers or cloches.

pests.name: Black bean aphid
pests.signs: Black aphids on stems and shoot tips
pests.control: Rub off by hand or spray off with water; encourage ladybirds.

wintering.notes: Clear plants after the first frost; leave the roots to add nitrogen to the soil.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – runner beans; seed packet

cropping.notes: Pick young and often.

lookOutFor: Cold, wet soil rots seeds; wait for warmth.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Seedlings eaten off at soil level
pests.control: Raise plants indoors and plant out when larger; check after dark.

pests.name: Black bean aphid
pests.signs: Clusters on shoot tips and under leaves
pests.control: Rub off by hand; encourage natural predators.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – French beans; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow in a wide, flat drill, about 5 cm apart each way.

cropping.notes: Pick regularly from the bottom of the plant up.

lookOutFor: Needs pea sticks or netting to climb.

pests.name: Pea moth
pests.signs: Small caterpillars inside the pods
pests.control: Sow early or late so flowering misses midsummer, or cover with fleece while in flower.

pests.name: Mice
pests.signs: Seeds dug up and eaten
pests.control: Start seeds in guttering or modules and plant out as young plants.

pests.name: Powdery mildew
pests.signs: White powder on leaves late in the season
pests.control: Water at the roots in dry spells; clear old plants promptly.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – peas; seed packet

conditions.hardiness: Half-hardy: shoots are damaged by frost

sowing.notes: Plant chitted seed potatoes: first earlies in late March, maincrop by early May.

cropping.notes: Earlies when the flowers open; maincrop when the foliage dies back.

lookOutFor: Earth up shoots as they appear to protect them from frost and stop tubers turning green.

pests.name: Potato blight
pests.signs: Brown patches on leaves and stems in warm, wet weather; tubers rot
pests.control: Grow resistant varieties, cut off and remove infected foliage, and lift tubers two weeks later.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Holes and tunnels in tubers
pests.control: Lift maincrops promptly in autumn; avoid heavy, wet ground.

pests.name: Common scab
pests.signs: Rough, corky patches on the skin
pests.control: Water well while tubers form and avoid adding lime before planting.

wintering.notes: Dry for a few hours, then store in paper sacks in a cool, dark, frost-free place.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – potatoes; seed potato supplier

sowing.notes: Plant sets with the tip just showing.
Autumn sets of overwintering varieties.
From seed, in modules.

cropping.notes: Lift when the leaves yellow and flop over.

lookOutFor: Birds pull up newly planted sets; cover with fleece until rooted.

pests.name: Onion white rot
pests.signs: Yellowing leaves and white fluffy mould at the base
pests.control: Remove affected plants and don't grow onions there again for many years.

pests.name: Onion fly
pests.signs: Wilting, yellow leaves and maggots in the bulb
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh; grow from sets rather than seed.

wintering.notes: Dry thoroughly in the sun, then store in nets somewhere cool and airy.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – onions; seed packet

sowing.notes: Plant sets with the tip just showing.

cropping.notes: Lift the clumps when the leaves turn yellow.

lookOutFor: Birds pull up newly planted sets; cover with fleece until rooted.

pests.name: Onion white rot
pests.signs: Yellowing leaves and white mould at the base
pests.control: Remove affected plants; avoid growing alliums there again for many years.

wintering.notes: Dry well, separate the bulbs and store somewhere cool and airy.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – shallots

conditions.soil: Free-draining; add grit to heavy soil

sowing.notes: Plant single cloves, pointed end up. Autumn planting gives the biggest bulbs.

cropping.notes: Lift when the lower leaves turn yellow.

lookOutFor: Needs a cold spell to form good bulbs.

pests.name: Rust
pests.signs: Orange spots on the leaves
pests.control: Space plants well for airflow; mild attacks rarely harm the bulbs.

pests.name: Onion white rot
pests.signs: Yellowing leaves and white mould at the base
pests.control: Remove affected plants and rotate crops.

wintering.notes: Autumn-planted cloves overwinter in the ground. After harvest, dry and store somewhere cool.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – garlic

sowing.notes: Sow in a seedbed or modules.

cropping.notes: Lift as needed through autumn and winter.

lookOutFor: Transplant when pencil-thick into deep dibber holes and fill them with water, not soil, for long white stems.

pests.name: Allium leaf miner
pests.signs: Lines of tiny white dots on leaves; twisted stems with brown pupae
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh in spring and autumn when the flies are active.

pests.name: Leek moth
pests.signs: White patches and holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh; remove damaged leaves.

pests.name: Rust
pests.signs: Orange spots on the leaves
pests.control: Space well for airflow; don't overfeed with nitrogen.

wintering.notes: Leave in the ground and lift as needed.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – leeks; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow thinly every few weeks for a steady supply.

cropping.notes: Pull when about pencil-thick.

lookOutFor: Easy to grow in a pot or between slower crops.

pests.name: Onion white rot
pests.signs: Yellowing leaves and white mould at the base
pests.control: Rotate crops; avoid ground where white rot has been.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – spring onions; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow very thinly every three weeks; thin to about 6 cm.

cropping.notes: Pull young for sweetness, or leave maincrops to size up.

lookOutFor: Stony or freshly manured soil gives forked roots.

pests.name: Carrot fly
pests.signs: Rusty-brown tunnels in the roots
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh; sow thinly so you don't have to thin, as the smell attracts the fly.

wintering.notes: Lift by late autumn on heavy soil and store in boxes of damp sand.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – carrots; seed packet

sowing.notes: Use fresh seed each year; germination is slow.

cropping.notes: Flavour sweetens after a frost.

lookOutFor: Slow to come up; mark the row with quick radishes.

pests.name: Parsnip canker
pests.signs: Orange-brown rough patches on the shoulders of the root
pests.control: Grow resistant varieties and sow a little later.

pests.name: Carrot fly
pests.signs: Tunnels in the roots
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh.

wintering.notes: Leave in the ground and lift as needed.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – parsnips; seed packet

sowing.notes: Each 'seed' is a cluster; thin to the strongest seedling.

cropping.notes: Pull when golf-ball to tennis-ball size.

lookOutFor: Early sowings may bolt in cold spells; choose bolt-resistant varieties.

pests.name: Birds
pests.signs: Seedlings pecked
pests.control: Cover with netting or fleece until established.

wintering.notes: Twist off the leaves and store in boxes of damp sand.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – beetroot; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow little and often; ready in about four weeks.

cropping.notes: Pick young; old roots turn woody and hot.

lookOutFor: Dry soil makes them split or run to seed.

pests.name: Flea beetle
pests.signs: Lots of small round holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fleece and keep the soil moist.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – radish; seed packet

cropping.notes: Pull early varieties at golf-ball size.

lookOutFor: A brassica: grow it with the cabbage family in your rotation.

pests.name: Flea beetle
pests.signs: Small holes in young leaves
pests.control: Cover with fleece and keep watered.

pests.name: Clubroot
pests.signs: Swollen, distorted roots and wilting plants
pests.control: Rotate brassicas; lime acid soil; don't bring in soil from infected ground.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – turnips; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow a short row every two weeks.

cropping.notes: Cut whole heads, or pick outer leaves from loose-leaf types.

lookOutFor: Runs to seed in heat and drought; some midday shade helps in summer.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Ragged holes and slime trails
pests.control: Check after dark, use barriers, and water in the morning rather than evening.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.signs: Green or black insects on leaves and roots
pests.control: Rinse off; encourage ladybirds and hoverflies.

wintering.notes: Hardy varieties can overwinter under cloches.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – lettuce; seed packet

sowing.notes: Late sowings crop through autumn and again in spring.

cropping.notes: Pick leaves young; cut-and-come-again.

lookOutFor: Bolts quickly in hot, dry weather; keep it watered and lightly shaded.

pests.name: Downy mildew
pests.signs: Yellow patches on top of leaves, grey mould beneath
pests.control: Thin for airflow and water at the base.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Holes in the leaves
pests.control: Check after dark; use barriers.

wintering.notes: Autumn sowings overwinter better under a cloche.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – spinach; seed packet

cropping.notes: Pick outer leaves and stems; plants keep producing.

lookOutFor: One of the easiest leafy crops, and colourful in a border.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Holes in young leaves
pests.control: Check after dark; protect young plants.

wintering.notes: Usually survives winter and crops again in spring.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – Swiss chard; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow in a seedbed or modules.

cropping.notes: Pick young leaves from the top down.

lookOutFor: Plant firmly; brassicas dislike loose soil.

pests.name: Pigeons
pests.signs: Leaves torn to the ribs, especially in winter
pests.control: Cover with netting held clear of the leaves.

pests.name: Cabbage white caterpillars
pests.signs: Holes in leaves, green caterpillars underneath
pests.control: Cover with fine mesh from spring; pick off eggs and caterpillars.

pests.name: Clubroot
pests.signs: Swollen roots, stunted and wilting plants
pests.control: Rotate brassicas; lime acid soil; raise plants in pots to give a strong start.

wintering.notes: Crops right through winter.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – kale; seed packet

sowing.notes: Spring, summer, autumn and winter types; sow at the time each needs.

cropping.notes: Cut when the heads feel firm.

lookOutFor: Plant very firmly and water in well.

pests.name: Cabbage root fly
pests.signs: Young plants wilt; white maggots at the roots
pests.control: Fit a collar around the stem when planting, or grow under mesh.

pests.name: Cabbage white caterpillars
pests.signs: Holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine mesh; check undersides for eggs.

pests.name: Clubroot
pests.signs: Swollen roots, stunted plants
pests.control: Rotate brassicas; lime acid soil.

wintering.notes: Winter and spring cabbages stand through cold weather.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – cabbages; seed packet

cropping.notes: Cut spears when the buds are tight; more follow.

lookOutFor: Tall plants may need staking in exposed gardens.

pests.name: Pigeons
pests.signs: Leaves torn in winter
pests.control: Net the crop.

pests.name: Cabbage white caterpillars
pests.signs: Holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine mesh in summer.

wintering.notes: Stands over winter to crop in early spring.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – broccoli; seed packet

sowing.notes: In modules; it dislikes root disturbance.

cropping.notes: Cut the main head while the buds are tight; side shoots follow.

lookOutFor: Check often in warm weather; heads open into yellow flowers quickly.

pests.name: Cabbage white caterpillars
pests.signs: Holes in leaves and heads
pests.control: Cover with fine mesh.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – broccoli; seed packet

cropping.notes: Cut while the curd is firm and white.

lookOutFor: Needs steady watering; a check in growth gives small, loose heads. Fold leaves over the curd to keep it white.

pests.name: Cabbage white caterpillars
pests.signs: Holes in leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine mesh.

pests.name: Clubroot
pests.signs: Swollen roots, stunted plants
pests.control: Rotate brassicas; lime acid soil.

wintering.notes: Winter types overwinter to crop in spring.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – cauliflowers; seed packet

cropping.notes: Pick sprouts from the bottom of the stem up.

lookOutFor: Firm the soil well and stake tall plants against winter wind.

pests.name: Pigeons
pests.signs: Leaves torn in winter
pests.control: Net the crop.

pests.name: Cabbage whitefly
pests.signs: Tiny white insects fly up when leaves are disturbed
pests.control: Usually harmless to the sprouts; remove badly affected lower leaves.

wintering.notes: Crops through winter.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – Brussels sprouts; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow seed on its edge in small pots.
Under a cloche once frosts are over.

cropping.notes: Pick at 10–15 cm, every couple of days in summer.

lookOutFor: One or two plants feed a family; water heavily at the base.

pests.name: Powdery mildew
pests.signs: White powder on the leaves in late summer
pests.control: Water at the roots in dry weather and remove the worst leaves.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Young plants eaten
pests.control: Plant out strong plants and protect them at first.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – courgettes; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow seed on its edge in small pots.

cropping.notes: Cut with a length of stalk before the first frost.

lookOutFor: Trailing plants need plenty of room, or train them up a strong support.

pests.name: Powdery mildew
pests.signs: White powder on the leaves late in the season
pests.control: Water at the roots; it rarely harms the fruit this late.

pests.name: Slugs
pests.signs: Young plants eaten
pests.control: Protect young plants after planting out.

wintering.notes: Cure the fruits in the sun for a week or two, then store somewhere cool and dry.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – pumpkins and winter squash; seed packet

sowing.notes: Needs warmth to germinate.

cropping.notes: Pick regularly before the fruits yellow.

lookOutFor: Greenhouse types need warmth; outdoor ridge types suit a sunny, sheltered spot.

pests.name: Powdery mildew
pests.signs: White powder on the leaves
pests.control: Keep the roots moist and the air moving.

pests.name: Red spider mite
pests.signs: Fine mottling on leaves and webbing, in greenhouses
pests.control: Damp down the greenhouse floor to raise humidity; biological controls are available.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – cucumbers; seed packet

sowing.notes: Needs warmth to germinate; earliest for a greenhouse.

cropping.notes: Pick as the fruits colour; ripen the last green ones indoors.

lookOutFor: Pinch out side shoots on tall (cordon) varieties and tie the stem to a cane.
Water regularly; uneven watering causes split fruit and blossom end rot.

pests.name: Tomato blight
pests.signs: Brown patches on leaves and stems; fruit turns brown and rots, outdoors in wet summers
pests.control: Grow blight-resistant varieties or grow under cover; remove infected plants.

pests.name: Blossom end rot
pests.signs: Sunken black patch at the base of the fruit
pests.control: Water regularly so the roots never dry out.

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.signs: Tiny white insects under leaves, in greenhouses
pests.control: Yellow sticky traps and good ventilation; biological controls are available.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – tomatoes; seed packet

sowing.notes: In deep modules or root trainers.

cropping.notes: Ready when the tassels turn brown and the juice of a squeezed kernel is milky.

lookOutFor: Plant in a block, not a single row, so the wind pollinates the cobs.

pests.name: Mice and birds
pests.signs: Seeds dug up; cobs pecked
pests.control: Raise plants indoors; net ripening cobs if needed.

pests.name: Frit fly
pests.signs: Twisted, stunted young shoots
pests.control: Raise plants in modules and plant out when larger.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – sweetcorn; seed packet

conditions.soil: Well-drained, fertile; or a large pot

sowing.notes: Needs about 20°C to germinate; a heated propagator helps.

cropping.notes: Pick green or leave to ripen to full colour and heat.

lookOutFor: Best in a greenhouse or a sunny, sheltered spot against a wall.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.signs: Clusters on shoot tips and under leaves
pests.control: Squash or rinse off; encourage ladybirds.

pests.name: Whitefly
pests.signs: Tiny white insects under leaves
pests.control: Yellow sticky traps and good ventilation.

wintering.notes: Plants can be kept indoors over winter and cropped again.

source: Check against: RHS Grow Your Own – chilli peppers; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow little and often; it runs to seed fast in hot weather.

cropping.notes: Pick young leaves; it regrows.

pests.name: Flea beetle
pests.signs: Small round holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh; keep seedlings watered so they grow away quickly.

source: Check against: RHS – salad rocket; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow after midsummer: earlier sowings tend to bolt.

pests.name: Flea beetle
pests.signs: Small round holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh; keep seedlings watered so they grow away quickly.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.signs: Young plants eaten, especially on damp nights
pests.control: Protect young plants and check for slugs after dark; encourage birds, frogs and beetles.

source: Check against: RHS – pak choi; seed packet

sowing.notes: Sow little and often.

cropping.notes: Pick when the size of a tennis ball, before it turns woody.

pests.name: Flea beetle
pests.signs: Small round holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh; keep seedlings watered so they grow away quickly.

source: Check against: RHS – kohlrabi; seed packet

pests.name: Flea beetle
pests.signs: Small round holes in the leaves
pests.control: Cover with fine insect mesh; keep seedlings watered so they grow away quickly.

pests.name: Clubroot
pests.signs: Stunted plants; swollen, distorted roots
pests.control: Lime acid soil and rotate crops; don’t bring in soil from elsewhere.

wintering.notes: Can stay in the ground over winter until needed.

source: Check against: RHS – swedes; seed packet

lookOutFor: Keep well watered all summer or the roots stay small.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.signs: Young plants eaten, especially on damp nights
pests.control: Protect young plants and check for slugs after dark; encourage birds, frogs and beetles.

wintering.notes: Cover with straw in hard winters.

lookOutFor: Self-blanching kinds grow best in a block, not a row.

pests.name: Slugs and snails
pests.signs: Young plants eaten, especially on damp nights
pests.control: Protect young plants and check for slugs after dark; encourage birds, frogs and beetles.

pests.name: Celery leaf miner
pests.signs: Brown blotches in the leaves
pests.control: Pick off affected leaves; cover with fine mesh.

cropping.notes: Pick green, or leave to ripen to red or yellow.

lookOutFor: Best in a greenhouse; outside only in a warm, sheltered spot.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.signs: Clusters of small green or black insects on shoot tips
pests.control: Squash by hand or wash off with water; ladybirds and hoverflies will follow.

source: Check against: RHS – sweet peppers; seed packet

sowing.notes: Needs warmth, about 20°C.

lookOutFor: Best in a greenhouse in the UK.

pests.name: Red spider mite

pests.control: Mist plants and keep the greenhouse humid.

source: Check against: RHS – aubergines; seed packet

cropping.notes: Wait two years after planting, then cut spears for six to eight weeks each spring.

lookOutFor: Plant crowns in a trench about 20 cm deep, roots spread out. A bed lasts twenty years.

pests.name: Asparagus beetle
pests.signs: Black-and-yellow beetles on the ferns
pests.control: Pick them off by hand.
